page.layout: One column of running text. Running head and page number at the top. Catchword and gathering signature at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Certitudo oraculi ducitur ab auctoritate Dei illud promulgantis, qui mentiri nescit, ut aut divina voluntate superiore causam requirere fas non est: sic nec ἐποχὴν[?] seu du-bitare licet, quando aliquid à Deo ipso pro-nunciatum esse constat.
Usus huius sentetiæ geminus est, ratione videlicet tam verorum Israelitarum, quàm Edomitarum, qui illorum hostes sunt. Seruit enim ad illos quidem consolā-dos,hos autem perturbandos & terredos.

Utignis & flamma non habet, cur sibi ab aridis stipulis metuat, sed hæ profectò habent cur extimescant ignem, à quo citò absumuntur: ita non est cur pij metuant Edomitas, falsos nimirum suos fratres, quia non deest illis patronus, aduersus quem nec consilium nec fortitudo est: sed hi enim-verò habent, cur illos metuant, quos ne attingere quidem impunè liceat. Notum est dictum: Non permisit quemquam nocere ipsis, & corripuit propter eos reges (dicens) Nolite tangere vnctos meos, & prophetis meis nolite malè facere, Psalm. 105.14.15.
Etsi autem παράδοξον[?] videtur, pij metuen-di sunt impijs: tamen id verissimum est.

page.notes: Greek words set in italic: "ἐποχὴν" (reading uncertain, marked) and "παράδοξον" (reading uncertain, marked). Printed spelling "sentetiæ" kept as printed, possibly a printing error for "sententiæ". "Seruit enim" appears with almost no space in the scan; written with a space. "dos,hos" has no space after the comma in the print and is kept as printed. Printed "Vsus" and "Vtignis" changed to Usus and Utignis per the u/v rule. The running head is "COMMENTARIA" as printed, without the page number. The catchword "&c" stands at the right foot and the signature "H 3" at the left.
